evidence.quote: This document does not define how the authorization server should determine the client's certificate during token introspection.
evidence.relevance: RFC 8705 explicitly excludes revocation re-evaluation and does not define per-request triple evaluation.

evidence.quote: DPoP does not ensure the integrity of the request payload or any request headers.
evidence.relevance: RFC 9449 limits proof to method and URI; no device-posture dimension.

evidence.quote: Cryptographic binding between DPoP and client authentication mechanisms is out of scope.
evidence.relevance: No normative mechanism binds DPoP to a device-posture signal.

evidence.quote: The resource server MUST respond with an HTTP 401 status code.
evidence.relevance: RFC 9470 defines only binary deny; no graduated outcome pathway.

evidence.quote: The authorization_details claim in an issued token represents the authorization at the time of issuance.
evidence.relevance: RFC 9396 authorization_details is static post-issuance; no per-request narrowing.

gaps.title: No Method-Level Downgrade on Posture Degradation

evidence.quote: The actions element is a list of strings representing the actions to be performed.
evidence.relevance: RFC 9396 actions are issuance-time; no mechanism to restrict HTTP method per-request on posture change.

evidence.quote: The resource server MUST NOT accept the access token for use with other protected resources.
evidence.relevance: RFC 9470 escalation path does not include method-level restriction as a distinct outcome.

gaps.title: No Normative Threat-Response Pathway for Cryptographic Threat Events

threat_event_types.rationale: HNDL exposes tokens to future CRQC decryption; active token sessions should be restricted to read-only pending re-enrollment with PQ-safe algorithm.

threat_event_types.description: Algorithm family deprecated by CA, national standards body, or IETF WG consensus
threat_event_types.rationale: Tokens bound to deprecated algorithm families retain structural validity but carry elevated cryptographic risk; method restriction with upgrade advisory is proportionate response.

threat_event_types.description: Public disclosure of side-channel or fault-injection attack capability against key type in use
threat_event_types.rationale: Cryptographic oracle attacks can recover private key material; full denial and token revocation are warranted.

evidence.quote: This standard specifies ML-DSA, a digital signature algorithm based on the hardness of the Module Learning With Errors (MLWE) problem, intended to be secure against attacks by quantum computers.
evidence.relevance: FIPS 204 ML-DSA provides the PQ-safe algorithm family toward which Algorithm-Agility Triggers drive re-enrollment.

evidence.quote: No resource is inherently trusted. Every asset must have its security posture evaluated via a PEP before a request is granted.
evidence.relevance: ZTA per-request evaluation requirement motivates synchronous threat-event response pathway.

evidence.full_citation: P.W. Shor, 'Algorithms for quantum computation: discrete logarithms and factoring,' Proc. 35th FOCS, 1994, pp. 124-134.
evidence.relevance: Shor's algorithm breaks RSA/ECDSA in polynomial quantum time; HNDL threat presupposes eventual CRQC availability.
